Manufacturer's official color name for this product variant. The manufacturer's official marketed colorway name, verbatim — most case manufacturers brand their colorways. If the manufacturer doesn't give a fancy name, fall back to a simple human-readable color ('Black', 'White', 'White / Silver'). Branded / collab colorways belong here when the rest of the hardware is unchanged. Examples: HYTE Y70 in Snow White → 'Snow White'. Fractal Design North in Charcoal Black → 'Charcoal Black'. HYTE Y70 Persona 3 Reload Edition → 'Persona 3 Reload Edition'. Do NOT put hardware sub-model differentiators like 'Momentum Edition', 'RC', or 'Flow' in manufacturer_color — those are either the variant or part of the series.

Product series name The manufacturer's product line / model name that groups related cases. Manufacturer and `form_factor` are stored separately and used as the default grouping, so do NOT repeat them in the series. The same family CAN span multiple form factors (`North` is its own series; `North XL` is a separate series, not a variant). Examples: 'Fractal Design North ATX Mid Tower' → series='North'. 'HYTE Y70 ATX Mid Tower Snow White' → series='Y70'. 'NZXT H3 Flow Micro ATX Mid Tower' → series='H3 Flow'.

Specific variant in the series Most cases should have an empty variant — color/finish belongs in `manufacturer_color`, not here. Only set a variant when a sub-model needs to be distinguished from the base model within the same (manufacturer, series, form_factor) group: limited / collab editions that change more than paint, refreshed revisions, or named sub-models. Examples: 'Fractal Design North ATX Mid Tower Black' → variant='' (color is the only difference). 'Fractal Design North Momentum Edition' → variant='Momentum Edition'. 'Fractal Design North XL RC' → variant='RC'. The variant must be unique within a (manufacturer, series, form_factor, manufacturer_color) group — if every case collapses to the same value, leave it empty.

Full product name Prefer manufacturer + product family + processor number/suffix. Exclude generic category words like 'processor' or 'CPU' unless they are part of the marketed family name. Exclude cache, frequency, and other trailing spec text. Example: Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus, AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D

Product series name Use the exact reference name first; if there is no reliable reference name, use the exact source product name. Return the normalized family bucket that groups nearby SKUs together — not the full SKU and not the bare tier alone. Include the family number when the naming scheme uses one. Do NOT include the manufacturer name (Intel/AMD) in Series — that belongs in `manufacturer`. Full SKU identifiers belong in `variant`. Reject broad marketing labels like 'Intel Core Ultra Processors (Series 2)' unless they exactly match the canonical family bucket. Examples: 'Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus' → series='Core Ultra 5 200'. 'Intel Core i7-14700K' → series='Core i7 14000'. 'AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D' → series='Ryzen 7 9000'. Wrong outputs for the same examples would be: 'Intel Core Ultra 5 200', 'Core Ultra 5', '250K Plus', or 'Series 2'.

Specific variant in the series Use the exact model number and suffix that identify the specific SKU inside the series family bucket. Examples: 'Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus' → variant='250K Plus' (with series='Core Ultra 5 200'). 'Intel Core i9-14900KS' → variant='14900KS'. 'AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D' → variant='9800X3D' (with series='Ryzen 7 9000').

Manufacturer's official color name for this product variant. The manufacturer's marketed colorway name when one exists; otherwise derive a simple human-readable color from the product images (do not infer color from words in the title). Common values: 'Black' (most stock boards), 'White', 'White / Silver'. Branded special editions belong here when the manufacturer markets them as a distinct colorway (e.g., 'HATSUNE MIKU EDITION'). Examples: standard ROG STRIX X870E-E in black → 'Black'. White ROG CROSSHAIR X870E GLACIAL → 'White' (GLACIAL is the model variant, not the colorway). Hatsune Miku ROG STRIX X870E-H Gaming → 'HATSUNE MIKU EDITION'. Do NOT put model descriptors like `HERO`, `APEX`, `EXTREME`, `GLACIAL`, `Creator` in manufacturer_color — those belong in the variant.

Product series name The manufacturer's sub-brand or product line that groups related boards. Manufacturer, chipset, and memory type are stored separately and used as the default variant grouping, so do NOT repeat any of them in the series. Examples: 'Asus ROG CROSSHAIR X870E HERO WIFI DDR5 ATX' → series='ROG CROSSHAIR'. 'Gigabyte X870E AORUS MASTER' → series='AORUS'. 'MSI MEG X870E GODLIKE' → series='MEG'. The series stays consistent across multiple chipset generations of the same product line.

Specific variant in the series The full board model identifier inside the series. It MUST include the chipset SKU as the manufacturer prints it (e.g., `X870E`, `X870E-E`, `X870E-PLUS`, `B650M-A`) plus any model descriptor that distinguishes it from siblings (`HERO`, `APEX`, `EXTREME`, `MASTER`, `Creator`, etc.). Include `WIFI` / `WIFI7` / `BT` tokens ONLY when they appear in the manufacturer's printed model name on the box; the full WiFi standard still goes in `wireless_networking`. Do NOT include the manufacturer, the broad series, the form factor, or memory type — those are stored separately. Examples: 'Asus ROG CROSSHAIR X870E HERO WIFI DDR5 ATX' → variant='X870E HERO WIFI'. 'Asus X870E-PLUS TUF GAMING WIFI7' → variant='X870E-PLUS WIFI7'. 'ASUS ROG CROSSHAIR X870E GLACIAL' → variant='X870E GLACIAL'. The variant must be unique within a (manufacturer, chipset, memory type) group — if two boards collapse to the same variant string, you are missing a model descriptor.
